gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-stack-sans-not: Blockletter stands up with a stretched middle and pencil-sketched lines that never press harder, precise and modern. Stack Sans Notch is sans-serif, open-curved and rod-straight.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-stack-sans-tex: Blockletter draws its letters with a pencil that never leans in, giving a stretched midsection and a precise, modern look. And Stack Sans Text is sans-serif, marker-like in line, with big-bodied lowercase that keeps its curve endings well apart.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-sulphur-point: Blockletter stretches its midsection and sketches every letter with a pencil that never presses harder, which makes it precise and modern. And Sulphur Point, a bulky sans with marker-like lines and gaps left open in its a, e and s, can take a larger size comfortably.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-ubuntu-sans: Pencil-sketched and stretched upright, Blockletter looks precise, while Ubuntu Sans is sans-serif with washer-sized lowercase eyes and strokes like bent copper pipe. Blockletter sketches best; Ubuntu Sans pipes best.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans draws its line like a ruler would, constant in width, with wide unclosed terminals. Under Blockletter's stretched, pencil-sketched headings, its x-height fills each line and the plain sans keeps the page steady.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-yaldevi: Blockletter looks drawn with a round-tipped pen, its midsection stretched and its lines never pressing harder, so headings feel precise and modern. Yaldevi, a sans-serif, takes over with outsized lowercase and an e whose eye opens clearly to the right.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-alexandria: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody a commanding, dripping presence at the top of the page. And Alexandria, a sans with wide open terminals and a lofty body with short stems above and below, steps in to keep things clean.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-amiko: Amiko reads modern, its lowercase strokes as high as a thick crayon mark and its terminals pointing outward like tongs. Bloody leads with big round bowls and a commanding feel; Amiko, a plain sans, simply carries the text.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-anek-devanagari: Big round lowercase bowls make Bloody commanding from the first word. And Anek Devanagari, a sans-serif with distinctly open letter mouths and a lofty middle zone, is what makes this pairing stand out.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-anek-kannada: Anek Kannada reads contemporary, its x-height reaching high like a squared-off woodblock letter, with terminals that stop far from the stem. Anek Kannada looks restrained beside Bloody's commanding, big round bowls, and each makes the other look sharper.
